[Acompanhante] and I are most interested in the six-hour Extended tour of the Lisbon in Perspective brochure from 10 am to 5 pm. Since our plane doesn't arrive in Lisbon until 9:05 am on May 1, we would want to book this tour for Saturday, May 2. Our hotel is [morada removida]. We are joining Globus Journeys that night for our welcome dinner at 6 pm so we would have both pick-up and drop-off at the hotel.

We do need to change the Belem portion of the tour. The Jeronimos Monastery, Belem Tower, and Discovery Monument are all part of our tour with Globus Journeys and while we would expect that your tour would be more informative, we think we don't need to do it twice. Would it be possible to skip those and spend the time instead, with other sights in the old town areas? [Acompanhante] and I have interests in seeing several things in the areas we will already be visiting. Some of these may already be things you planned on showing us on your tour. And some may be new adventures. And we may be listing too many to make sense of the freed-up time. I'll summarize the additional possibilities.

Alfama area - Museum of Portuguese Decorative Arts
Bairro Alto area - Sao Roque Church with the Chapel of St John the Baptist for the gold and blue lapis lazuli columns; Jacaranda trees, if blooming, at the Largo do Carmo square; Gothic Arches of the Convento do Carmo
Chiado area - Paris en Lisboa fabric store on Rua Garrett; Manteigaria to watch the pastry chefs make pastel de nata; Bertrand Bookstore (operating since 1732) on Rua Garrett; A Vida Portuguesa on Rua Nova de Almada at #72 for Portuguese gifts
Baixa area - Black & White cobbled sidewalk at Rua do Comercio; Tiles on the Church of St. Nicholas (Igreja de Sao Nicolau); MUDE, Lisbon's museum of 20th century design and fashion; Calcada Worker Memorial bronze statue on the square Praca dos Restauradores; Ginjinha Sem Riyal for Eduardinho liqueur; Cod shop on Rua Dom Antao de Almada off the Praca da Figueira
Tiles - we both love the tiles and are disappointed that the National Tile Museum is temporarily closed. We will be going to the Palacio dos Marqueses de Fronterira the day before to see the tiles there. So we want to make sure we see tiles - we love the sidewalk picture of tiles in your brochure!

We appreciate you working with us to trade out Belem for other sights. Just let us know what you think will work.
